# Wagner Logistics to Add Nearly 80 Jobs with New High-Volume Logistics Operation in Liberty

 Wagner Logistics 

Oct 14, 2026, 08:54 ET

NORTH KANSAS CITY, Mo., Oct. 14, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Wagner Logistics, a nationwide provider of third-party logistics, today announced it has signed a multi-year agreement with a Kansas City-area manufacturer to launch a new manufacturing support and warehouse operations program in Liberty, Mo.

The new operation includes two leased warehouse facilities in the Liberty area totaling more than 830,000 square feet. Wagner expects to add 79 new local jobs over the next two years, starting immediately. The company will also make a multi-million-dollar investment in equipment, infrastructure and automated trailer loading and unloading technology to support the operation.

"This is exactly the kind of operation where Wagner's strengths come through," said Brian Smith, President and Chief Executive Officer of Wagner Logistics. "It requires speed, flexibility, close coordination and the ability to design a solution around what the customer actually needs."

Hollingsworth Logistics is adding 150 jobs and consolidating its operations near San Antonio with a new 340,000-square-foot warehouse at Park35. The expansion will retain 224 current employees and supports growing regional warehousing demand.

A Michigan-based logistics company is expanding its operations near San Antonio, Texas, with plans to add 150 jobs and consolidate two existing facilities into a 340,090-square-foot warehouse along Interstate 35.

Hollingsworth Logistics Group has signed a seven-year lease at Park35, a growing industrial development in Schertz, northeast of San Antonio. The expansion will retain 224 existing positions, bringing the company's planned local workforce to 374 employees.

By Joshua Burd

Rockefeller Group has filled one of two new industrial buildings in Salem County, leasing 530,000 square feet to a growing New Jersey-based logistics firm.

The tenant, Metropolitan Warehouse and Delivery, recently took occupancy at the Carneys Point facility after expanding and moving from its existing location in Perth Amboy. # A. Duie Pyle Opens 78,760-SF Warehouse in Camp Hill, Pennsylvania

 October 6, 2026 

 

A. Duie Pyle has opened a 78,760-square-foot warehouse in Camp Hill, Pennsylvania, creating an integrated logistics center that combines warehousing with the company’s existing less-than-truckload operations on one campus.

The new warehouse, located at 485 Terminal St., sits directly adjacent to Pyle’s LTL service center at 475 Terminal St. By connecting the two operations, the West Chester, Pennsylvania-based logistics company is bringing inventory storage and regional transportation into a single facility designed to reduce freight handoffs and accelerate distribution.

The Camp Hill hub connects customers with Pyle’s transportation network across the Northeast, Mid-Atlantic and Ohio while providing warehouse capacity close to several major regional freight corridors.

The facility has convenient access to Interstate 81, Interstate 76, Interstate 83 and U.S. Route 15, positioning inventory within reach of major population and distribution markets throughout Central Pennsylvania and the surrounding region.

A Delavan-based third-party logistics and fulfillment company has significantly expanded its Midwest warehouse capacity after moving into a new distribution facility in Kenosha.

Becker said the facility can handle nearly 7 acres of inventory under one roof. G10 shares the building with food manufacturer Eagle Foods.

G10 invested about $2 million in the Kenosha buildout, which Becker said covered racking, automation and staffing costs.

# Averitt adds 100,000-sq.ft. Warehouse to Mississippi Freight Campus

Written by WarehouseArc Newsroom • August 28, 2026

Averitt has opened a 100,000-square-foot warehouse beside its existing 57-door LTL terminal in Richland, Mississippi, putting distribution, fulfillment and asset-based freight operations on the same logistics campus.

The Jackson Distribution & Fulfillment facility opened August 24 at 109 Diane Drive, near the intersection of Interstates 20 and 55.

Rather than operating solely as a dedicated warehouse for a single customer, the building is configured as a multi-tenant facility where Averitt is offering space without long-term warehouse contracts.

That gives the 3PL capacity for customers seeking temporary inventory space as well as more conventional distribution and fulfillment operations. Averitt is marketing the building for requirements including overflow inventory, seasonal storage and emergency staging, with customers able to adjust the amount of space they use as requirements change.

The operational proposition extends beyond the additional square footage.
